x: Your results have been obtained by conscientious training and you have set a plendid example to our younger members. Bob Newson is also showing remarkable progress. With good, steady training, the results are bound to follow.

… the field had sorted itself out and coming up the hill the first time, Eric Hall, who had held the lead, was passed by Bob Newson, but once back on the Common, Eric again took the lead and was not again headed, thus winning the cup for the second year in succession in the good time of 56m. 41secs.…
McFarlane (Police) were in the lead, followed by Brian Shepherd, George Checkley, Bob Newson and Percy Wright. On the last lap McFarlane got away and was first home in 80m.

Over the second half Bob Newson came through exceptionally well to finish 5th in 84m.36s Having lost Demmon, we had to go back to 27th and 33rd positions to complete the team with a score of 65 points to Highgate's 40, and Surrey W.C. 61.
Green, Syd James, Bob Newson, Brian Shepherd, McGreechan and Beecham. Crossing Purley Way, Syd had moved up to Eric and Evans with Bob coming along like a rocket.
As a result of the race, three of our walkers were selected to represent Middlesex at Southport, George Checkley 9th, Bob Newson 11th and Hugh McGreechan 12th.
At 4 miles Syd James was 15th, Eric Hall 18th, George Checkley 30th, Hugh McGreechan 36th and Bob Newson 40th. It was pleasing to see Bennard Eglington home from Germany and competing.
Syd James and Bob Newson were 3rd and 4th in 2hrs 13mins. 44secs and the "Demon-chest-King" 7th. The match, six a side, resulted in a win for us by 40 points to Surrey's 61, with the Police 81.

Next for us in 8th position was George Checkley, another grand performance and our scoring team was completed by Bob Newson, trying gallantly even in the last yard to catch and pass the Woodford man a pace ahead, and Bernard Eglington on leave from Germany.
The first six Londoners were to be selected for a visit to Paris and competition was very keen with Syd James, Eric Hall, Bob Newson, George Checkley and George Beecham all in the field.
Bob Newson and Hugh McGreechan held their positions right through and Bob certainly earns credit for finishing 4th in 2hrs. 36mins. 53secs. Mac was 5th in 2.37.29 and Len Demmon 10th in 2.44.45.

Hugh McGreechan was well up all the way followed by Bob Newson with Beecham and Norman a little way back. After a bad spell on the homeward journey, Mac recovered and beat George Coleman near home for 5th place.

…was Bernard, on leave as already mentioned, who only failed by 37 secs. to beat 3 hours. 4th only 23 seconds behind was Bob Newson, definitely showing good improvement over distances and quite capable of fulfilling Jack Bidgood's prophecy when he said at the finish "A couple of years and the Champio…

At the moment most of our distance men have a Middlesex qualification and our team consisted of George, Bob Newson, Hugh McGreechan, Len Demmon, Bob Readman, Fred Rolfe and Cyril Yescombe, and of course Harry Shields.

Bob Newson ran into a bad spell during the third lap and both he and George Beecham were passed by Harry. Halfway round this lap we heard George Beecham had stopped and dashed back to him and had to transport him to the dressing room.
Of a field of 25, Eric Hall was first home in 48mins.14secs. Bob Newson 2nd in 49.41 and E.
Eric Hall was first home in 39mins. 6 secs. followed by Ted Smith, Syd James and Bob Newson and the match resulted in a win for us by 52 points to 119.
Doubleday (2.35) managed to keep Bob Newson away for third place. The winner's time was 22 mins. 56 secs. and it was pleasing to see our President a proud competitor.

Hipkins of the Stock Exchange was also up with the leaders and down Copse Hill the positions remained unchanged with Dicky Green, another 'Change walker, Bob Newson and Tony Clark closely following those out in front.

A trio of Hugh McGreechan, Bob Newson and Norman Guilmant were at this time some three minutes behind with George Beecham, Harry Shields and Cyril Yescombe completing the team a further 2 minutes back.
Bob Newson walked a very sound 20 miles indeed and came through beautifully in the second half of the race. George Checkley, our third man to finish, will not regard this as one of his best races.
George Beecham who took it steady at the start, walked well to finish 6th and Bob Newson over the last four miles, passed Norman Guilmant and really got moving to finish 8th.

Behind these two an interesting battle was going on for third place between Bob Newson, Hugh McGreechan and Norman Guilmant. The last named tried hard to steal a lead but Bob and Hugh would not let him get away.

We badly needed the assistance of Bob Newson and George Checkley, but in the circumstances, the lads did very well. In the handicap team race we took 2nd place Eric, Norman, George Beecham and Fred Rolfe sharing the prizes.

In the three miles Dave McMullen 4th and Bob Newson 5th collected 45 points and we had a lead of 4 points. In the final race of 2 miles, Ted Smith was 2nd and Joe Coleman 6th making a grand total of 173 points and maintaining our lead of 4 points to win.
From the start Bob Newson and Hugh McGreechan walked a steady race followed by George Beecham and Harry Shields with Fred Rolfe bringing up the rear.

George Checkley however, who seems to relish such conditions, had moved into an early lead in front of our second man Bob Newson, with Norman Guilmant also moving strongly and it looked rosy at halfway.

With fine efforts from Eric Hall, Ted Smith, George Checkley and Bob Newson, the latter practically killing himself to take Stan over the last couple of laps, we won the team race from Woodford Green.
George Checkley walked really well to win in 40m.12s. with Bob Newson second, Syd James (whom we are pleased to see out again) third and Eric Froude, still improving, fourth.
George Checkley walked strongly in the second half of the race, gaining several places and finishing just in front of Bob Newson who walked evenly throughout.
Packing well, our lads put their team in the first twelve positions with Ted Smith 7th, Dave McMullen 8th, George Checkley 9th, Syd James 11th and Bob Newson 12th!

Bob Newson and Dave McMullen were close behind, followed by G.Beecham, H.McGreechan and J.Coleman. At a further check three miles later, the team position was almost the same, with Belgrave 39pts to Met.W.C's 55 and Sheffield still a long way behind.
George Checkley walked soundly throughout, never seeming to falter; Bob Newson was a powerful third man and Hugh McGreechan prevailed over George Beecham for fourth position.

Splendid backing up by Bob Newson, Ray Switzer and George Beecham ensured us of a clear team victory over Leicester W.C. by a margin of 12 pts.
Meanwhile, George Beecham, revelling in the sunshine, came through to fourth with Hugh McGreechan and Bob Newson completing our scoring team in 6th and 7th positions.
Hugh McGreechan was 4th in 3h.49m.38s., Bob Newson 5th in 3.52.27, George Checkley 11th in 4.0.42, Bernard Eglinten 12th in 4.3.21, Fred Rolfe 15th in 4.7.35 and Harry Shields 16th in 4.8.12.
Moreover most of our men reported fit and well, although we should have liked to have seen Bob Newson, Syd James and Roy Switzer in the field.
